text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Spanish markets maintain confidence that peseta will be in euro.
- Aznar names Popular Party deputy Fernando Lopez-Amor, managing director of Spanish state television RTVE.
EL MUNDO
- Microsoft chairman Bill Gates says Internet is unstoppable revolution during trip to Madrid.
DIARIO 16
- Monica Ridruejo, RTVE managing director who resigned, is fed up with politic use of Spanish state television, at expense of neglecting its debt.
ABC
- Despite offensive from northern countries, Spanish economy continues firmly along track toward European Monetary Union.
LA VANGUARDIA
- Hooded youths attack justice of peace courtroom in northern Spain.
- Catalan leader Jordi Pujol reiterates that demographic stagnation is most worrying problem in Cataluna.
- Barcelona and Real Madrid draw in football match, Real Madrid eliminated from Cup.
CINCO DIAS
- Government elimates 15 year limit for civil servants, on voluntary leave of absence, to return to their jobs.
- Naval construction company Astilleros creates shock plan which it intends to put into action on February 17.
EXPANSION

- Fear that Social Security department will be unable to meet its promises on pensions has sparked dramatic increase in savings. Total amount invested in private pension plans and funds grew 40.6 percent in 1996.
- Flex chairman Antonio Betere sells his shares in BCH and Zaragozano to finance restructuring of mattress business.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Fashion house Adolfo Dominguez will be launched on stock market with estimated valuation of 25 billion pesetas or 2,941 pesetas per share.
- Government assures will not accept any shady deal to join Europe's Monetary Union.
- Industry Ministry decides to replace Inespal chairman Javier Alvarez Vara.
- Employers' group calls for simplifying and lowering of personal income tax.
